label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common), early in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 steps where the agent chose a2 and reached S2 by the common transition (99.7% of mass), and only in the first ~45 trials of an episode: it never fires on trial 50 or later. Magnitude falls steadily with episode trial. Restricting to ep_trial < 20 still covers 99.7% of the top activation quartile but only 7% of the bottom quartile, and windows show values going 1.00, 0.97, 0.67 over consecutive trials. Magnitude also tracks high value. It does not fire at D1 or GO, after a1, or on rare a2 -> S1 trials, and after a1 -> S2 (rare) it is almost silent (0.3% of mass). All variables used (this trial choice and reached state at D2, trial number) are observed at D2. Without the time condition, precision drops to 0.36 (F1 0.53).

issues: Every factual claim checked out. All activation mass is at D2 (D1 and GO: 0 active steps). The predicate scores dev F1 0.911 and mass recall 0.996; with ep_trial >= 50 it covers 0 activation mass. With ep_trial < 20 it covers 99.7% of the top activation quartile and 7.4% of the bottom quartile, as the explanation says.

Small scattered gap: a1 -> S2 (rare) does fire sometimes (D2 & state==2 & action==1 & ep_trial<45: precision 0.02, 0.3% of mass; one test miss reaches 0.65 of max). So 'does not fire after a1' is very nearly true but not strictly. The feature really tracks reaching S2 early in the episode, and that almost always means via a2.
The ep_trial < 45 cutoff gives the best F1, but the falloff is gradual rather than a hard edge: 40-49 still fires at a 0.043 rate, and ep_trial < 42 gives P 0.88 / R 0.94.

About 15% of predicted steps are false positives. These are partly explained by low model value: adding value >= 7.9 raises dev F1 from 0.911 to 0.934 and test F1 from 0.903 to 0.930. This refines the predicate rather than refuting it; the explanation already says magnitude tracks high value.
No systematic false-positive class tied to the good state or to reward history was found (good==1 within the predicate holds only 7% of mass). The predicate uses no future variables.
